html:
Military trial of Lieutenant William Calley at Fort Benning, Georgia, for his part in the My Lai massacre. He was found guilty on 29 March 1971.

Twenty-five officers and men were charged in all, but Calley was the only one convicted. The court found him guilty of the murder of at least 22 civilians and sentenced him to life at hard labour. Calley said he had followed orders. The trial drew wide public attention, and many Americans, including some who opposed the war, felt he was being made a scapegoat.

President Nixon moved him from the stockade to house arrest while he appealed. The sentence was cut to 20 years, then 10. Calley served about three and a half years under house arrest before he was freed in 1974.

The case showed how rarely atrocities in the Vietnam War were punished.
